claims.statement: FPT/GHEC-only source requires repository admin to enforce Pages HTTPS; plan-dependent repository availability is separate from published-site access and no protection change is authorized.

Source states Pages/custom-domain HTTPS support when custom domain correctly configured, and github.io sites created after June 15 2016 receive HTTPS automatically. Availability/default serving is distinct from tested HTTP redirect enforcement.

Pages should not serve sensitive password/payment transactions. FPT private repository does not imply private website; GHEC sites default public except managed-user/private-access cases. Source warning's GHES Public Pages branch is not part of this cloud-only article applicability.

Certificate note attributes common-name maximum 64 characters to RFC3280, then requires entire domain strictly less than 64. Preserve maximum-versus-strict-boundary wording discrepancy; neither standard interpretation nor boundary behavior independently verified.

Enforce HTTPS UI selection is configuration only; require actual HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, certificate/hostname validity and asset retrieval observations to prove effective behavior. No site visited or settings changed.

Custom-domain save starts DNS eligibility check, certificate job/Let's Encrypt request and installation on TLS termination servers; check mark follows success. Asynchronous queued/requested/configured states are not a valid live certificate receipt.

Source suggests removing/retyping/saving custom domain to cancel/restart stalled provisioning. This is a native domain mutation with continuity/takeover implications, not permission for automatic recovery; no DNS or domain changed.

HTTP images/styles/scripts on HTTPS pages are mixed content that may weaken security or break assets. Source remediation changes asset URLs to HTTPS; endpoint support/content equivalence must be verified rather than blanket rewrite all URLs.

Jekyll layouts and HTML head/body are suggested asset locations; source search for http:// is a diagnostic aid, not exhaustive generated-content assurance or proof every match is an insecure subresource.
Illustrative stylesheet/script/image/link HTTP-to-HTTPS table is reference only; examples do not certify third-party host reachability, ownership or asset licensing.

Extra apex A/AAAA/ALIAS/ANAME or chosen-subdomain CNAME records may prevent certificate provisioning. Historical table gives Pages address examples and owner.github.io targets; no current DNS recommendation, live resolution proof or authority to overwrite unrelated service records.
Source DNS/TLS/domain/privacy and RFC links remain separately scoped. No accepted control, source completeness certification, published assurance, rights clearance or native rollout follows.
